title: Crispy Potatoes Without Deep Frying: Three No-Fry Techniques from Techniquely with Lan Lam
summary: This video explains the science of achieving crispy potatoes without deep frying and demonstrates three no-fry methods. Lan Lam contextualizes the idea that crispness comes from a dry starch network formed when water is driven off and heat and oil render that network into a browned, crunchy exterior. The three methods shown are: roasted smashed potatoes (steam-roasted, then smashed for maximum surface contact and browning), home fries pre-treated with an alkaline boil (baking soda in water to rough up exterior before roasting with aromatics), and oven fries coated with a cornstarch slurry (microwave-thickened slurry to build a protective shell, then steamed and browned). Each method emphasizes not cooking and crisping simultaneously, but sequencing steam, starch development, and browning to achieve a crispy, fluffy interior without deep frying.

sections.title: - What Makes French Fries So Good?
sections.description: Matt Card's roasted smashed potatoes are prepared by selecting small potatoes (1.5–2 inches) with thin skins, boiling with water, and covering with foil at 500°F to steam the potatoes so they cook evenly. After cooking, the potatoes are lightly oiled and smashed to expose more surface area, seasoned with salt, pepper, and thyme, re-oiled for even coating, and roasted again until browning and crispness develop on all exposed starches.

sections.title: - Crispy Home Fries
sections.description: Andria Gir's home fries begin by pre-treating the exterior: potatoes are boiled with baking soda in the water to raise the surface pH, which helps the exterior break down and form a coating of free starch. The potatoes are then tossed in a mixture of salt, butter, and a pinch of cayenne, and partially cooked to create a paste-like coating that coats the potatoes. Baking on a hot sheet pan follows, with onions added for flavor; the finished result is deeply browned with a crisp exterior and a tender interior.

sections.title: - Thick-Cut Oven Fries
sections.description: The oven fries technique uses a cornstarch slurry to build a protective shell around potato wedges. The slurry is created by whisking water into cornstarch and microwaving until it thickens. The wedges are coated with the slurry and, like the other methods, are covered with foil to trap steam for cooking through, then uncovering to brown and crisp. The result is a crispy exterior with a tender interior and visible frizzled edges of the cornstarch coating.
